params.body:
## Why

`VehicleTextService::systemPrompt()` wrote both vehicle texts with one instruction set. The only difference was a single line ("For the key vehicle_own_description, go deeper into the equipment and options"), so the model produced two variations of the same consumer sales letter: the Stocklist text picked up the garage's own story, and the own-fleet text was no warmer than the trade copy.

## The two audiences

- **`vehicle_description` (Beschrijving stocklist)** is trade copy on the Stocklist marketplace. The reader is another dealer. Factual and businesslike, about the vehicle: equipment, condition, history. The selling garage stays in the background: no company name, no story about the garage, no consumer sales pitch.
- **`vehicle_own_description` (Beschrijving eigen wagenpark)** goes to the garage's own channels. The reader is the end customer. Here the garage speaks in its own voice: warmer in tone, the equipment explained in terms of what the driver gets from it, and deeper on options than the trade copy.

## What the prompt now says

The shared lines are unchanged: the JSON-object reply contract with exactly the requested keys, the language, "use only those facts, invent nothing", no test drive, no markdown or HTML, 1000-10000 characters, the "Information:" and warranty handling, and the dealer note (`$dealerNote`), which still applies to every text.

Added per key, and only when that key is requested (the button calls the service per field, and instructions for a text that is not being written are noise):

- `vehicle_description`: named as trade copy for the Stocklist marketplace, reader is another dealer; factual and businesslike; the selling garage kept out of it.
- `vehicle_own_description`: named as the garage's own channel, reader is the end customer; own voice, warmer tone, equipment in terms of what the driver gets; go deeper on the options than the trade copy does.

## Scope of the administrator setting

`$extraInstructions` is the `ai_vehicle_prompt` setting. It is now appended only when `vehicle_own_description` is being written, with its scope stated in the prompt itself ("apply it to vehicle_own_description only, never to vehicle_description"), so the garage's voice cannot leak into the trade copy.

Two things worth knowing before this is merged, because they do not match the assumption that this setting is the garage's own company text:

1. **The garage's company text is a different setting.** `ai_dealer_company_info` ("Standaard info die altijd mag opgenomen worden in de commerciële tekst van het voertuig", per dealer, Instellingen > AI) already reaches only the own-fleet text, because `Vehicle::aiFactsOwn` folds it into the facts for that key alone. Nothing about that changed here.
2. **`ai_vehicle_prompt` is a platform-wide setting, visible only to a Stocklist admin** (`@if(Auth::user()->isAdmin())` on the AI tab, stored with `dealer_id` null and read with `whereNull('dealer_id')`), and it was labelled "AI prompt add-on" - a label that suggests it applies to both texts, which is also what rule S1-4.7 said ("een extra instructie voor de AI-prompt die voor alle dealers geldt"). Restricting it to the own-fleet text is therefore a real narrowing, not a clarification. The label was clearly wrong once the scope narrowed, so it now names the scope in all five languages (nl: "AI-promptaanvulling (enkel beschrijving eigen wagenpark)"). If the intent is that this add-on should still steer the trade copy as well, say so and the condition comes out again - one line in `systemPrompt()`.

Business rules S1-4.6 (the two readers, and one text at a time) and S1-4.7 (the scope of the administrator instruction) are updated in `docs/bedrijfsregels/11-s1-wagen-invoeren-en-beheren.md`; `92-testdekking.md` and `bedrijfsregels.html` regenerated with `bin/rules-coverage --write` and `bin/rules-page`.

## Checked

`php artisan test --filter='VehicleText|OpenAI|SmokeTest|RulesCoverage'` on a private MySQL database: 3 failures, the same three as on `origin/main` without this change (two `IntegrationSmokeTest` seal expectations and one smoke page needing a `notifications` table that the committed schema dump does not carry), and 16 assertions more than before. No OpenAI call in the tests: the existing stub of `callModel` records the messages.

New tests in `tests/Feature/VehicleTextServiceTest.php`: the prompt names the reader of each text and keeps the contract lines; the administrator instruction is scoped to the own-fleet text; asking only for `vehicle_description` mentions neither the own-fleet instructions nor the administrator instruction; asking only for `vehicle_own_description` does not mention the trade-copy reader.
params.title: AI texts: trade copy for the Stocklist, the garage's own voice for its own channels
